summary.text: Celeste Maloy is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election, running in the newly drawn 3rd District after representing the old 2nd District since November 2023. A Cedar City native and attorney, she worked as a soil conservationist and then in public lands and water law before serving as counsel to Rep. Chris Stewart, whose seat she won in a 2023 special election. She sits on the Appropriations and Natural Resources committees, chairs the Congressional Western Caucus, and is running on tax cuts, border security and giving Utah more control over federal lands.

paragraphs.text: Born in Cedar City, Utah, in 1981 and raised in Hiko, Nevada; graduated from Pahranagat Valley High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in agriculture from Southern Utah University in 2003 and a J.D. from Brigham Young University in 2015.
Began her career as a soil conservationist, which her House website says lasted about a decade working with Utah families and farmers.

After law school, worked as a deputy Washington County attorney, a public lands attorney for the Utah Association of Counties and a staff attorney for the Washington County Water Conservancy District.
Served as chief legal counsel to Rep. Chris Stewart before running for his seat.

Won the Republican convention on June 24, 2023, then the September 5, 2023 special Republican primary (38.8%) over Becky Edwards and Bruce Hough, and the November 21, 2023 special general election (56.8%) to succeed Stewart; took office November 28, 2023.
Re-elected in November 2024 with 58.0% of the vote over Democrat Nathaniel Woodward.
In the 2023-2024 term served on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Small Business.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) serves on the Committee on Appropriations, as vice chair of the Interior, Environment and Related Agencies subcommittee and as a member of the Energy and Water Development and Legislative Branch subcommittees, and on the Committee on Natural Resources (Federal Lands; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries subcommittees).
Chairs the Congressional Western Caucus and, according to her House website, holds co-chair roles on the Bipartisan Build America, Bipartisan Wildfire and other caucuses.
